boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten Georgia Tech study environments for quiet reading, group work, archival research, multimedia production, and project development, with current access constraints from official university sources.

cards.entity_name: Crosland Tower Sixth-Floor Quiet Reading Room
cards.title: Settle In for Quiet Work on Six
cards.subtitle: An open quiet-study floor with power, data, and campus views
cards.notes: Bring a device and charging cable, choose an open seat, and preserve the floor’s quiet atmosphere during focused reading or writing.
cards.short_summary: A large, open reading environment designed for silent individual work above campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Georgia Tech Library identifies its sixth floor as a large, open quiet-study space available 24 hours a day, with power, data, and views.
cards.source_title: Collaborative & Quiet Study Spaces | Georgia Tech Library
cards.access_notes: The official study-spaces page says the sixth-floor quiet space is available to anyone 24 hours a day; building-entry controls may still apply.

cards.entity_name: Crosland Tower Seventh-Floor Quiet Reading Room
cards.title: Read Above the Campus on Seven
cards.subtitle: Quiet seating, power, and elevated Midtown views
cards.notes: Use this floor for concentration-heavy work, plug into the available power, and keep conversations elsewhere to respect quiet-study use.
cards.short_summary: An upper-level reading room combining quiet expectations with broad campus and city views.
cards.evidence_claim: Georgia Tech Library identifies its seventh floor as a large, open quiet-study space available 24 hours a day, with power, data, and views.
cards.source_title: Collaborative & Quiet Study Spaces | Georgia Tech Library
cards.access_notes: The official study-spaces page says the seventh-floor quiet space is available to anyone 24 hours a day; building-entry controls may still apply.

cards.title: Spread Out on the Grove Level
cards.subtitle: Book-lined reading space beside collaborative seating and powered stairs
cards.notes: Choose the reading room for book work or shift to the nearby collaborative areas when a project benefits from conversation and shared materials.
cards.short_summary: A book-centered reading room connected to flexible collaborative areas on the Library’s Grove Level.
cards.evidence_claim: Georgia Tech Library states that the Grove Level includes a new book reading room and collaborative spaces with available power and data ports.
cards.source_title: Collaborative & Quiet Study Spaces | Georgia Tech Library
cards.access_notes: Use is subject to current Georgia Tech Library building access and hours; the official page does not state a reservation requirement.

cards.title: Build Out the Idea on Crosland Two
cards.subtitle: Large tables and rolling whiteboards for hands-on scholarly projects
cards.notes: Bring sketches, models, or a group problem, then rearrange the rolling boards and work surfaces to match the scale of the project.
cards.short_summary: A flexible, low-tech studio for brainstorming, drawing, model-building, and collaborative project work.
cards.evidence_claim: Georgia Tech Library describes this second-floor Crosland studio as a collaborative space with large work tables, rolling whiteboards, and high stools.
cards.source_title: Innovation & Ideation Studio | Georgia Tech Library
cards.access_notes: Located on Crosland Tower’s second floor and usable whenever the Library is open, according to the official page.

cards.title: Take Graduate Work to Crosland Six
cards.subtitle: Quiet carrels, comfortable seating, monitors, and reservable breakout rooms
cards.notes: Use the carrels for solo work; reserve a breakout room when a small academic group needs a monitor and conversation-friendly space.
cards.short_summary: A graduate-only study community that separates quiet individual seating from small-group rooms.
cards.evidence_claim: Georgia Tech Library says the Graduate Student Community provides quiet-study carrels, comfortable seating, and six reservable breakout rooms.
cards.source_title: Graduate Student Community | Georgia Tech Library
cards.access_notes: BuzzCard access is limited to Georgia Tech graduate students. Breakout rooms require instant reservation and are for academic or scholarly use only.

cards.title: Pair Reading Time with the Sci-Fi Shelves
cards.subtitle: A first-floor Crosland lounge surrounded by circulating speculative fiction
cards.notes: Settle in with course reading or browse the nearby circulating collection when research touches science-fiction history, criticism, or culture.
cards.short_summary: A recognizable library lounge embedded in Georgia Tech’s circulating science-fiction collection.
cards.evidence_claim: Georgia Tech Library locates the Science Fiction Lounge on Crosland Tower’s first floor and documents its broad circulating science-fiction collection.
cards.source_title: Science Fiction Lounge | Georgia Tech Library
cards.access_notes: Use is subject to current Georgia Tech Library building access and hours; collection borrowing follows Library eligibility rules.

cards.title: Work Where the Media Tools Are
cards.subtitle: Multimedia computers and production spaces on Price Gilbert’s third floor
cards.notes: Use the open computing zone for editing, or complete the required training before planning work in a reservable audio or video studio.
cards.short_summary: A production-oriented work environment for multimedia research, editing, recording, and design.
cards.evidence_claim: Georgia Tech Library says the Media Scholarship Commons offers multimedia computers, reservable production studios, editing space, and student support.
cards.source_title: Media Scholarship Commons | Georgia Tech Library
cards.access_notes: The Price Gilbert third-floor computing zone needs no reservation. Audio and video studios require training quizzes before reservation.

cards.title: Plan a Primary-Source Research Session
cards.subtitle: Crosland’s supervised workspace for Archives and Special Collections
cards.notes: Search the finding aids, request offsite materials ahead of time, and arrive ready to follow the room’s handling and personal-item rules.
cards.short_summary: A staffed research room where archival records, rare materials, and Georgia Tech history can be consulted.
cards.evidence_claim: Georgia Tech Library identifies this first-floor Crosland room as the public access point for Archives and Special Collections research.
cards.source_title: Archives Reading Room | Georgia Tech Library
cards.access_notes: Open Monday-Friday, 11 a.m.-4 p.m. Appointments are not required, but many offsite materials must be requested at least 24 hours ahead.

cards.title: Reserve a Screen-Ready Study Room
cards.subtitle: A named Price Gilbert room within the Library reservation system
cards.notes: Book ahead, bring the reservation email, and check in promptly at the room display so the system does not release the space.
cards.short_summary: A photo-documented reservable room suited to focused academic meetings or collaborative study.
cards.evidence_claim: Georgia Tech Library depicts Price Gilbert 4214 on its study-room page and states that study rooms offer laptop connections and LCD screens.
cards.access_notes: Eligible students, faculty, and staff may reserve study rooms up to two weeks ahead. Check in within 10 minutes or the reservation is canceled.

cards.title: Rehearse Spoken Work in Clough 342
cards.subtitle: An acoustically treated room for podcasting, voice work, and assignments
cards.notes: Reserve the room for a spoken-media assignment, bring the emailed check-in code, and arrive early enough to complete the display check-in.
cards.short_summary: A reservable academic room whose sound treatment supports narration, podcasting, and voice-based projects.
cards.evidence_claim: Georgia Tech Library names Clough 342 as a podcast room with acoustic panels for podcasting, voice work, and related projects and assignments.
cards.access_notes: Reservation and display check-in are required. The official page says failure to check in within 10 minutes causes cancellation.

warnings: The title’s “Claimed by 9am” phrase is editorial framing; no card asserts that these spaces fill by that time.
Coordinates and map URLs are null because room-level geodata was not verified from the cited official pages.
Library access and hours can vary by academic calendar, holiday, and BuzzCard status; consult current Library hours before visiting.
